title: Digital Asset Accounting
answer: Blockchain to ledger reconciliation, token valuation, contract auditing, decentralised treasuries and impairment.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Blockchain to Ledger Reconciliation
children.blurb: Blockchain to ledger reconciliation is the process of matching on-chain transaction records with internal accounting ledgers for digital assets.

children.name: Valuing Illiquid Tokens
children.blurb: Valuing illiquid tokens covers digital assets that do not trade on an active market with reliable volume.

children.name: Auditing Smart Contracts
children.blurb: Auditing smart contracts is the practice of reviewing the code, state transitions, and economic logic of programs that execute on a blockchain.

children.name: Accounting for Decentralised Treasuries
children.blurb: Accounting for decentralised treasuries covers the recording, valuation, and reporting of assets held by DAOs, protocol treasuries, and other on-chain entities that manage funds through smart contracts and multisig wallets.

children.name: Impairment of Unique Digital Assets
children.blurb: Impairment of unique digital assets covers how entities test and write down the carrying value of non-fungible tokens, digital collectibles, virtual land, in-game items, and similar one-of-a-kind intangible assets recorded on a blockchain.

sections.body: Digital asset accounting applies artificial intelligence to the practical work of recording and reporting blockchain based holdings. AI systems now pull transaction data from public blockchains and match it against general ledger entries, flagging missing or duplicated transfers. For token valuation, machine learning models combine on-chain trading volume, liquidity depth, and comparable asset prices to produce daily marks for assets that rarely trade. Smart contract auditing tools use static analysis and pattern matching to find common vulnerabilities such as reentrancy and access control errors. Decentralised treasury tools simulate cash flows across multisig wallets and governance proposals. Impairment testing for unique digital assets uses automated price feeds and rarity based pricing models to suggest write-downs.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The most reliable work is reconciliation for major public chains like Ethereum and Bitcoin, where transaction data is complete and well structured. Token valuation is far from solved, especially for illiquid tokens with no active market, and any model output depends heavily on the assumptions fed into it. Smart contract auditing can catch known bug patterns but cannot prove that a contract is correct, and human auditors still review all findings. Accounting for decentralised treasuries lacks a single accepted standard, so firms often treat governance tokens and protocol owned liquidity inconsistently. Impairment of unique digital assets remains subjective because many non-fungible tokens have no observable market price, and write-downs often rely on appraisals or last sale data that may be stale.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader should start with Blockchain to Ledger Reconciliation, because every later step depends on knowing which assets are actually held. Valuing Illiquid Tokens then turns those reconciled holdings into balance sheet values, and it is the page to consult for pricing methods when no exchange price exists. Auditing Smart Contracts sits alongside valuation, since the code that controls token transfers and treasury functions must be checked before relying on reported balances. Accounting for Decentralised Treasuries brings reconciliation and valuation together at the entity level, covering multisig wallets, governance tokens, and protocol owned assets. Impairment of Unique Digital Assets is the narrowest page, focused on non-fungible tokens and the specific rules for writing them down when their value falls.
